nodes.label: 01.jev Study
nodes.rationale: October Jev study replacing the deleted 2026-09-jev/ (git 932e704).

nodes.label: new-study Skill
nodes.rationale: Creates numbered study folders (NN.topic/) in a standard format so every experiment has README/CLAUDE/AGENTS/docs scaffolding and the root README table stays in sync.

nodes.label: DEV_LOG_TEMPLATE
nodes.rationale: Lets work resume after interruption by reading the file: goal, current state, plan, change history, decisions.

nodes.label: HANDOVER_TEMPLATE
nodes.rationale: Transfers implemented logic to the next owner: data flow, step logic, external deps, design decisions with alternatives, caveats.

nodes.label: Reference Index (external materials)
nodes.rationale: External sources live in reference/; self-written summaries belong in ../notes/.

nodes.label: lab Repository Rules
nodes.rationale: Personal scratch repo, not production code.

nodes.label: lab Experiment Monorepo
nodes.rationale: An experiment record, not product code: reproducibility and records over polish; failed experiments keep their conclusions.

nodes.label: NN.topic Folder Numbering
nodes.rationale: Next number = highest existing [0-9][0-9].* folder + 1, two digits; replaces the older YYYY-MM-topic convention.

nodes.label: Last-Modified Date Update Rule
nodes.rationale: Any change inside the study folder must bump README's 최종 수정일; status changes update both project and root README.

nodes.label: Template Placeholder Substitution
nodes.rationale: Fill {placeholders} in README/AGENTS with today's date; leave docs/plan/templates placeholders untouched because they are templates. Verified by grepping for '{'.

nodes.label: MANUAL Marker Preservation
nodes.rationale: Content below <!-- MANUAL: --> survives /sync-agents regeneration so hand-written context is not overwritten.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md Hierarchy Rule
nodes.rationale: Directory additions update that directory's AGENTS.md and parent Subdirectories table, never overwriting MANUAL content.

nodes.label: worklog-discipline Auto-Documentation Rules
nodes.rationale: Docs are updated automatically alongside work without user request; core block is injected/replaced by the plugin, project extensions section is preserved.

nodes.label: Devlog Rule
nodes.rationale: Feature start creates docs/plan/active/{YYYYMMDD}_{feature}_devlog.md; direction changes logged in its change-history table.

nodes.label: Document Location Rule (all docs under docs/)
nodes.norm_label: document location rule (all docs under docs/)
nodes.rationale: Folder root keeps only README/CLAUDE/AGENTS and code; notes are numbered NN.topic.md and registered in README table.

nodes.label: Handover Rule
nodes.rationale: Feature completion produces a handover doc and handover-index entry; on handover, docs move from active/ to completed/.

nodes.label: Worklog Rule (docs/worklog/YYYY_MM_DD.md)
nodes.rationale: Every completed task appended with author, target files, what/why, verification; minimal headers (### per item only).

nodes.label: Disposable Code by Default
nodes.rationale: Tests/abstractions/error handling only on explicit request; global test-first rule disabled; verify by running scripts.

nodes.label: Independent Top-Level Experiment Folders
nodes.rationale: One top-level folder = one experiment; no cross-folder imports or shared module extraction.

nodes.label: New Experiment Convention (NN.topic via /new-study)
nodes.rationale: New folder requires README (question/status/conclusion) and a row in root README project list; update row on status change.

nodes.label: Ending an Experiment Procedure
nodes.rationale: Set status, fill conclusion (the real asset), generalize lessons into notes/.

nodes.label: Self-Contained Projects / No Root Environment
nodes.rationale: Stacks differ per experiment, so each project pins its own deps (uv/.python-version, package.json/.nvmrc).

nodes.label: Copy-First, Promote to shared/ After 3 Repeats
nodes.norm_label: copy-first, promote to shared/ after 3 repeats

nodes.label: LLM backbone + trained decision head approach
nodes.norm_label: llm backbone + trained decision head approach

nodes.label: Parallel sampler
nodes.rationale: No decoding loop; all questions evaluated simultaneously and independently on shared state, giving 70-500ms latency but no inter-question dependency.

nodes.label: System One Model
nodes.rationale: Named after Kahneman's System 1: fast intuitive judgment ('expert decision within 5 seconds without research') at machine scale; models consumed by code, not humans, need types, speed/cost, and confidence.

nodes.label: Type safety / schema guarantee
nodes.rationale: '0% hallucination' is true by definition (schema matching guaranteed), not empirical; semantic errors remain.

nodes.label: LLM logit readout approach
nodes.rationale: Directly implements the hypothesis that Jev is rebranded constrained decoding; zero-shot but suffers position bias and ~26-option limit.

nodes.label: Reduce all types to k-way choice
nodes.norm_label: reduce all types to k-way choice
nodes.rationale: noul = 2-way, score = ordered k-way read by expectation; one scorer handles all three primitives.

nodes.label: Bidirectional encoder prevents state KV reuse
nodes.norm_label: bidirectional encoder prevents state kv reuse
nodes.rationale: 'single forward pass' means one call; compute scales with number of questions.

nodes.label: Shared scalar scorer
nodes.rationale: Option count k is not in parameter shapes, so unseen label sets/counts work without retraining; but training is mandatory (no zero-shot).

nodes.label: rlcd_loss (Laya RLCD)
nodes.rationale: Gaussian-policy REINFORCE in logit space with group-mean baseline (GRPO-like) plus soft CE; issue #741 measured no gain over soft-CE alone.

nodes.label: Confidence-threshold routing (auto / human review / reasoning LLM)
nodes.norm_label: confidence-threshold routing (auto / human review / reasoning llm)

nodes.label: Guo et al. 2017 (On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks)
nodes.norm_label: guo et al. 2017 (on calibration of modern neural networks)

nodes.label: Calibration
nodes.rationale: Jev's value comes from branching on confidence, so calibration (not accuracy) is the key verification point of the study.
